title: Family unhappy with review into death after tasering; Police face no charges, relatives say
article: The family of a man who died in police custody has been told there will be no charges laid in the death of Gordon Walker Bowe after an altercation with officers last year.

The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team has been investigating the actions of four Calgary police officers in the death of the Castlegar resident who travelled back and forth to Calgary for work. His family was told Wednesday the officers will not be charged in the death.
The team, which investigates police use of force complaints that involve serious injury or death, is scheduled to release the conclusion of its investigation today.
John Chernenkoff, Bowe's father-in-law, has been closely following the investigation and said he feels there are still too many loose ends.
"Why beat the piss out of him?There are a lot of questions that still are unanswered to my satisfaction," said Chernenkoff.
The incident happened in early November when police were called to a break and enter. When they arrived, Bowe was found in an unoccupied basement on 42nd Street S. E.
There was a struggle with police and a Taser was deployed, though it's not clear if it zapped him. Police noticed he was in medical distress and he was rushed to hospital, where he died.
From the beginning, Chernenkoff has been skeptical of police, telling the Herald days after the death that the man's bruising seemed, in his opinion, to be the result of a severe beating.

Bowe, 30, was hours from returning home to B. C. when he packed his bags and called home to say he was soon on his way, his family has said. But for some reason, Bowe ended up in the unoccupied basement.
Calgary Police Association president John Dooks said Wednesday that the officers, who have remained on duty during the investigation, were fully co-operative.
"I'm satisfied that the results of the investigation speak for themselves," said Dooks.
Dooks believes the death could be attributable to excited delirium or substance abuse, but he had not been briefed on the investigation's conclusion.
"We do know the officers had to use physical restraint to constrain this guy so the only other conclusion is the offender, Mr. Bowe, died as a result of a medical crisis," said Dooks.
Dooks said the death will not be tied to the Taser because one prong of the stun gun did not make contact with Bowe.

"He was subdued and restrained, but he didn't die as a result to blows being issued or kicks or anything like that. It's not the result of any excessive use of force, he died because of his medical condition," said Dooks.
Nine months later, Chernenkoff still alleges it's the officers' fault.

"My belief is the actions of the Calgary police caused his death. They said he was co-operative and submissive when they got there. Why did they beat the hell out of him? Because he was bruised and beaten pretty bad."
ASIRT executive director Clifton Purvis said the cause of death has been identified, but he would not discuss the matter.
"The outcomes of our investigation will be revealed (today)," said Purvis.
Bowe lived with his common-law wife in Castlegar and together they raised two young children.
